experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim and snorkeling among the rock formations.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local wineries in the Lagoa DOC wine region, the heart of Algarve winemaking. Tour the vineyards, learn about indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco, and enjoy guided tastings of crisp whites, rosés, and robust reds paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most photographed sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos, arched rock formations, and secret beaches along the dramatic Algarve coastline, combining adventure with breathtaking natural beauty.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Local Seafood Dinner
experiences.description: Visit the windswept Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of Europe, for a dramatic Atlantic sunset. Afterward, dine at a traditional tasca in Sagres village, savoring freshly grilled cataplana (seafood stew), percebes (barnacles), and local Algarve wine in an authentic fishing village atmosphere.
experiences.location: Sagres & Cabo de São Vicente, Vila do Bispo

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Oyster Tasting
experiences.description: Take a guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park of tidal channels, barrier islands, and wildlife. Stop at a local oyster farm to taste freshly harvested oysters paired with chilled Algarve white wine, and explore the pristine barrier island beaches accessible only by boat.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. €6-8, ~1.5 hours). Check in to Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24h petrol station kiosk near the bus terminal or a kebab shop near the hostel (under €5)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Faro–Lagos bus ticket online to save time. The hostel is a short walk from Lagos bus station. Keep luggage light for easy transit. Exchange some euros before arrival or use ATMs at Faro Airport.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy the hostel's communal breakfast area. Take a slow morning walk along Rua Dr. Faria e Silva into the historic old town of Lagos. Explore the charming cobblestone streets, the Igreja de Santo António, and the old city walls — all free to wander.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, a long golden beach just east of Lagos (15-min walk or short bus ride). Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing on one of the Algarve's most beautiful and uncrowded beaches. Bring water and snacks from a local supermarket (Lidl or Pingo Doce nearby).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Lagos marina at sunset. Explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril for budget tapas bars and cervejarias. Enjoy a cold Super Bock beer and petiscos (Portuguese tapas) at a local bar.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or pastel de nata + coffee at a local pastelaria (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed supermarket lunch on the beach — bread, cheese, fruit, water (€4-5)
meals.dinner: Petiscos and beer at a local cervejaria on Rua 25 de Abril (€8-12)

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a free Lagos tourist map from the hostel reception. Buy a reusable water bottle to save money throughout the trip. September weather is warm and sunny — perfect beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Praia Dona Ana, one of Lagos's most iconic beaches with dramatic golden cliffs and turquoise water. It's a 20-minute walk from the hostel. Arrive early to beat any crowds and enjoy the stunning scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal cliff path from Praia Dona Ana toward Praia do Camilo and Ponta da Piedade — a breathtaking series of sea caves, arches, and grottos. This free coastal walk is one of the Algarve's highlights. Optionally rent a kayak at Ponta da Piedade to explore the sea caves (€15-20/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos old town. Visit the Mercado de Escravos (Slave Market Museum, €3 entry) before it closes. Then enjoy dinner at a local tasca (traditional Portuguese tavern) in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria near the hostel — coffee and toast with butter and jam (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket eaten on the cliffs (€4-5)
meals.dinner: Prato do dia (dish of the day) at a local tasca — typically includes soup, main, bread, and drink (€8-10)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the cliff walk. Bring sunscreen and a hat. The cliff path can be narrow in places — take care near edges. Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the afternoon light for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus (Rede Expressos or Eva Bus, ~€4) to Sagres, the dramatic southwestern tip of Portugal. Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry), a historic 15th-century fortress perched on a windswept promontory with stunning Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of continental Europe (3km from Sagres or take a taxi for €5). The lighthouse and dramatic cliffs are awe-inspiring. Watch the waves crash against the rocks below. Browse the small artisan market near the lighthouse for affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Relax at the hostel and socialize with fellow travelers in the common area. Head out for a budget dinner in Lagos town center.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at a café near the Lagos bus station before departure (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or grab a bifana (pork sandwich) from a café in Sagres village (€3-4)
meals.dinner: Grilled sardines or bacalhau (salt cod) at a local restaurant in Lagos (€9-12)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. Buses from Lagos to Sagres run several times daily; check the Eva Bus schedule in advance. The round trip takes about 1.5 hours total.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia da Luz, a charming beach village 6km west of Lagos (local bus ~€2 or 30-min walk along the coast path). The beach has calm, clear water and a relaxed village atmosphere. Explore the small whitewashed village and its Roman ruins (Museu Arqueológico, free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Praia da Luz beach, swimming and relaxing. Walk the short cliff path east of the beach for panoramic views. Return to Lagos in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting evening in Lagos. Visit a local wine shop or bar offering Alentejo and Algarve wines by the glass. Try local varieties like Antão Vaz or Aragonez. Many wine bars offer tasting flights for €8-12.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café (€2-4)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood sandwich or prego (steak sandwich) at a beach café in Praia da Luz (€5-7)
meals.dinner: Light dinner of cheese, charcuterie, and local wine at a wine bar in Lagos old town (€10-14)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Luz is quieter than Lagos beaches — great for a relaxed day. The wine tasting evening is a perfect introduction to Portuguese wines before more dedicated tastings later in the trip. Ask hostel staff for their favorite wine bar recommendations.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus to Portimão (Eva Bus, ~€3, 30 minutes). Walk across the bridge to Ferragudo, a picturesque fishing village with a castle, colorful boats, and a lovely beach. Explore the village streets and visit the Castelo de São João do Arade (exterior free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha in Portimão, one of the Algarve's most famous beaches with impressive rock formations and golden sand. Spend the afternoon swimming and exploring the beach caves and rock formations on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Portimão's waterfront and visit the Museu de Portimão (€3 entry, free on Sundays), a fascinating museum about the sardine canning industry. Return to Lagos by bus. Dinner in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at the hostel or a local café (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Grilled fish at a local restaurant in Ferragudo near the waterfront (€8-11)
meals.dinner: Cataplana (traditional Algarve seafood stew) at a budget restaurant in Lagos — look for lunch-menu prices at dinner (€10-13)

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is far less touristy than Portimão and well worth the short detour. The Museu de Portimão is one of the best free/cheap museums in the Algarve. Keep bus tickets for the return journey.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves, the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve (bus from Lagos via Portimão, ~€5-6 total, 1 hour). Visit the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry) with panoramic views over the surrounding countryside and orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves old town — the Gothic cathedral (free entry), the Roman bridge, and the charming riverside. Visit the Museu Arqueológico de Silves (€2.10 entry). Walk through the local market area and browse fresh produce.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting at a local quinta (wine estate) near Silves or at a wine shop in town. The Algarve has a growing wine scene — try local Negra Mole red wine. Return to Lagos by bus in the early evening.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria in Lagos before departure — coffee and croissant (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a local tasca in Silves — prato do dia with soup and drink (€8-10)
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at the hostel's recommended restaurant or cook a simple meal using the hostel kitchen (€5-8)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is one of the most historically rich towns in the Algarve and often overlooked by tourists. The castle is excellent value. Check bus connections carefully — services between Silves and Lagos can be infrequent. Consider combining the Portimão bus with a local connection.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning in Lagos. Sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Visit the Mercado Municipal de Lagos (local market) on Rua Lancarote de Freitas for fresh fruit, vegetables, local honey, and artisan products. Great for budget shopping and local atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle from a local shop near the hostel (€10-15/day) and cycle to Praia do Porto de Mós, a beautiful and relatively quiet beach south of Lagos. Enjoy the afternoon swimming and exploring the rock formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return bikes and freshen up. Join a hostel-organized social event or pub crawl (often free or very cheap for hostel guests). Meet fellow travelers and explore Lagos's nightlife on Rua 25 de Abril.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and pastries from the market (€3-4)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach with market produce and supermarket snacks (€4-5)
meals.dinner: Burger or prego at a casual restaurant before the evening out (€7-9)

day_by_day.notes: The municipal market is best visited in the morning when it's most lively. Cycling is a great budget way to explore the coastline. Check with the hostel about any organized social events — these are great for meeting people and often include discounts at local bars.

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus to Albufeira (Eva Bus from Lagos, ~€6, 1.5 hours). Explore the old town of Albufeira — the whitewashed streets, the fishermen's beach (Praia dos Pescadores), and the clifftop viewpoints. Visit the Igreja Matriz de Albufeira (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Oura or Praia de Santa Eulália east of Albufeira for an afternoon of beach relaxation. These beaches have beautiful clear water and are less crowded in September. Walk the coastal boardwalk between beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Albufeira's famous Strip (Avenida Sá Carneiro) for budget dining and drinks. Return to Lagos by bus in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at a café in Lagos before departure (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at a local restaurant near Praia dos Pescadores in Albufeira (€9-12)
meals.dinner: Pizza or pasta at a budget restaurant on the Strip in Albufeira before the bus back (€8-10)

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira can be very touristy but the old town retains genuine Portuguese charm. September is ideal as the summer crowds have thinned. Check the last bus back to Lagos and plan accordingly — don't miss it!

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated wine tasting day. Take a morning bus toward the Alentejo wine region border or visit a local Lagos wine shop for a guided tasting session. Alternatively, book a half-day wine tour from Lagos to a nearby quinta in the Algarve wine region (budget tours from €25-35 including tastings).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine experience with a visit to Adega Cooperativa do Algarve or a local wine producer near Lagos or Portimão. Learn about indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole, Crato Branco, and Arinto dos Açores. Purchase a bottle or two of local wine at producer prices.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening with your purchased wine on the hostel terrace or rooftop (if available). Share wine with fellow travelers and swap travel stories.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café (€2-4)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery or a nearby café — cheese, bread, and local products (€6-9)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal in the hostel kitchen using local ingredients from the market (€5-7)

day_by_day.notes: Book wine tours in advance through the hostel or local tour operators. Many wineries offer free or low-cost tastings if you visit independently. The Algarve wine region is less famous than Alentejo but produces excellent and affordable wines. Bring a small bag to carry wine bottles safely.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Tavira, often called the most beautiful town in the Algarve (bus from Lagos via Faro, ~€9-11, 2 hours). Explore the Roman bridge, the castle ruins (free entry), and the charming old town with its distinctive four-sided rooftops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry to Ilha de Tavira (€1.50 each way), a stunning barrier island beach within the Ria Formosa Natural Park. Spend the afternoon on this pristine, unspoiled beach — one of the best in the Algarve. The water is calm and crystal clear.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tavira for a sunset stroll along the riverfront. Enjoy dinner in Tavira before catching the bus back to Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at Lagos bus station (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on Ilha de Tavira beach or buy from the island's beach café (€5-8)
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood dinner at a riverside restaurant in Tavira — look for the prato do dia (€9-12)

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is a long day trip from Lagos — start early. The last bus back to Lagos may require a connection in Faro or Portimão. Check schedules carefully. Ilha de Tavira is one of the Algarve's hidden gems and absolutely worth the journey. Bring cash as the island ferry may not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — revisit your favorite Lagos beach or try Praia do Barranco, a hidden gem accessible via a short cliff walk from Lagos. Spend a leisurely morning swimming, snorkeling, and soaking up the last of the Algarve sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for souvenir shopping in the old town. Browse the local shops for affordable Portuguese products: local wine, ginjinha (cherry liqueur), flor de sal (sea salt), almond sweets (Dom Rodrigo), and handmade ceramics. Stick to local shops rather than tourist traps for better prices.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best budget restaurant you've discovered during the trip. Splurge slightly on a nice bottle of local Algarve wine to celebrate the end of the trip. Return to the hostel for packing and final preparations.

meals.breakfast: Slow breakfast at a local café — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, toast, and coffee (€4-6)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach café or supermarket picnic (€4-6)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your favorite Lagos restaurant — treat yourself to a full meal with wine (€15-20)

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully, especially wine bottles — use clothing as padding. Check hostel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for the next morning. Confirm your transport to Faro Airport for the return journey.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Boutique Taghostel (store luggage if needed). Take a final morning walk through Lagos old town to say goodbye to the city. Visit any last sights you may have missed — the Ponta da Bandeira Fort (€3 entry) by the marina is quick and worthwhile.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, take the bus from Lagos to Faro Airport (Eva Bus, ~€6-8, 1.5 hours). Arrive at the airport with plenty of time for check-in and security. Browse the airport shops for any last-minute Portuguese products.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the beaches, wines, and culture of the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and coffee at a Lagos café — a fitting farewell (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or pack snacks from a supermarket for the journey (€5-8)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time carefully and work backwards to plan your Lagos departure time. The Lagos–Faro bus journey is approximately 1.5 hours. Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for the bus journey plus airport check-in. Keep all receipts and travel documents organized for the journey home.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-booked airport transfer or taxi (~1 hour) to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos. Check in, freshen up, and grab a late-night snack near the hostel if hungry. Rest and prepare for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour café or convenience store near Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, or grab a pastel de nata and a drink from a late-night bakery in Lagos old town.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid long taxi queues at night. Faro to Lagos is approximately 75 km. Consider downloading the Rede Expressos bus app as a backup option. Keep Day 2 light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café. Take a gentle orientation walk through Lagos old town — explore the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets. Visit the Igreja de Santo António if open.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, Lagos's longest and most accessible beach (10-minute taxi or 20-minute walk). Spend the afternoon relaxing on the golden sands, swimming in the warm Atlantic, and getting your first taste of the Algarve coastline. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella for comfort (~€10).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Lagos marina at sunset. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the old town. Return to the hostel for an early night.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or a local pastelaria near the hostel — espresso, fresh orange juice, and a croissant or tosta mista (~€5-7).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach bar at Meia Praia — grilled fish sandwich, salad, and a cold Sagres beer (~€12-15).
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant or Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos old town — try the cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) or grilled sea bass (~€20-28 per person).

day_by_day.notes: September is an excellent time to visit — crowds thin out after August but the sea is still warm (around 22°C). Pick up a local SIM card or activate roaming for navigation. The hostel reception can provide maps and local tips.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short taxi or local bus to Ponta da Piedade, Lagos's most iconic landmark. Explore the dramatic golden limestone rock formations, sea arches, and grottos along the clifftop walking path. Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat the heat and enjoy the best light for photos. The walk takes about 45-60 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Ponta da Piedade, take a short boat trip from the small dock below the cliffs (~€15-20 per person) to explore the sea caves and hidden grottos up close. Afterward, relax at Praia do Camilo, a stunning small beach tucked between the cliffs, accessible via a wooden staircase.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by late afternoon. Explore the Mercado de Lagos (municipal market) if still open. Enjoy a sunset drink at a rooftop bar or terrace bar in the old town before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café — yogurt, fruit, and coffee (~€5-8).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks from a local deli/supermarket (Pingo Doce is nearby) to enjoy at Praia do Camilo — save money and enjoy the beach setting (~€6-8).
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco or A Forja in Lagos — try the arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) or grilled dourada (sea bream) with local wine (~€22-30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the Ponta da Piedade clifftop walk — some paths are uneven. Apply sunscreen generously. The boat trips from the dock are informal and run throughout the day; no booking needed but arrive early in peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day experience: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim. Take a bus or taxi to Praia da Marinha (approximately 35 km east of Lagos, near Lagoa). Begin the famous Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos) — a 5.7 km clifftop trail offering breathtaking views of golden limestone cliffs, hidden coves, and turquoise waters. Start at Praia da Marinha and hike toward Praia de Vale Covo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha beach for a well-deserved swim in the crystal-clear waters surrounded by dramatic rock formations. This beach is consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful. Spend 2-3 hours swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by late afternoon. Freshen up at the hostel. Explore the vibrant Friday evening atmosphere in Lagos old town — browse local craft shops and enjoy the lively bar scene on Rua 25 de Abril.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel before departure — toast, eggs, and coffee (~€6-8).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy on the trail or at the beach — grab supplies from a local supermarket the night before. Alternatively, there is a small beach café at Praia da Marinha (~€10-14).
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso or Restaurante Bon Bon (casual option) in Lagos — try the piri-piri chicken or fresh grilled tuna steak with local vegetables (~€18-25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail is moderately challenging — wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring at least 1.5 liters of water per person. The trail is exposed with little shade, so start early (9:00 AM) to avoid midday heat. The bus from Lagos to Praia da Marinha runs via Portimão — check Eva Transportes schedules. A taxi is more convenient (~€25-30 one way).

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour — morning session. Join a guided wine tour departing from Lagos or Lagoa (the heart of the Lagoa DOC wine region, ~25 km from Lagos). Visit the first winery of the day, such as Adega do Cantor or Quinta dos Vales. Tour the vineyards, learn about the unique Algarve terroir, and taste the estate's signature whites and rosés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine tour with a visit to a second winery, such as Quinta da Penina or Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa. Enjoy a guided cellar tour, learn about the winemaking process, and participate in a structured tasting of reds, including the local Negra Mole and Castelão grape varieties. Many tours include a light lunch with local cheeses, charcuterie, and bread paired with wine.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon. Relax at the hostel. Head out for a leisurely evening stroll and dinner featuring Algarve wines you discovered during the tour.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hostel or a café near the hostel before the tour departs (~€6-8).
meals.lunch: Wine and food pairing lunch included in the vineyard tour — local cheeses, presunto (cured ham), olives, and bread paired with estate wines (typically included in tour price or ~€15-20 extra).
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — order a bottle of Lagoa DOC wine you discovered on the tour, paired with cataplana de peixe (fish stew) or grilled octopus (~€22-30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour in advance, especially on weekends in September. Tours typically cost €45-75 per person including transportation, guided tastings, and a light lunch. Designated driver or group transport is included — do not drive after wine tastings. The tour operator can arrange pickup from Lagos.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente. Take a bus or taxi to Sagres (~30 km west of Lagos). Visit the impressive Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress perched dramatically on a clifftop. Explore the historic windrose (Rosa dos Ventos) and learn about Portugal's Age of Discovery. The views of the Atlantic from the fortress walls are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or walk 6 km to Cabo de São Vicente — the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Stand at the edge of the continent and watch the powerful Atlantic waves crash against the 75-meter cliffs. Browse the small market stalls selling local crafts and dried fish. Spend time at Praia do Beliche, a sheltered beach near Sagres, for a late afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by early evening. Sunday evenings in Lagos are relaxed — enjoy a quiet dinner and perhaps a glass of port wine at a wine bar.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria in Sagres upon arrival — coffee and pastéis de nata (~€4-6).
meals.lunch: Restaurant Nort or A Sagres in Sagres town — fresh grilled fish of the day (peixe do dia) with boiled potatoes and salad, a classic Portuguese Sunday lunch (~€15-20 per person).
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Camilo or Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — try the bacalhau à brás (shredded salt cod with eggs and potatoes) or grilled sardines with cornbread (~€18-24 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The Eva Transportes bus runs from Lagos to Sagres several times daily (~€4 each way, 1 hour). A taxi is faster (~€25-30 one way). Sunday bus schedules may be reduced — check timetables in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning. Sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Spend the morning exploring Lagos's local markets and artisan shops. Visit the Mercado de Lagos (municipal market) for fresh local produce, fish, and regional products. Browse the craft shops along Rua 25 de Abril for handmade ceramics, azulejos (tiles), and cork products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour — afternoon session. Take a taxi or bus to Praia de Benagil (approximately 30 km east of Lagos). Join a guided kayak tour to paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave — one of the world's most photographed sea caves, featuring a stunning natural skylight. The tour typically lasts 2-3 hours and includes stops at multiple sea caves and hidden beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and share photos and stories from the kayak adventure.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a café in Lagos old town — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, toast, ham, cheese, and coffee (~€8-12).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near Praia de Benagil before the kayak tour — sandwich, salad, and fresh juice (~€10-14).
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon or Tasca do Celso in Lagos — try the arroz de pato (duck rice) or fresh grilled sea bass with local wine (~€20-28 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour well in advance — it is one of the most popular activities in the Algarve and spots fill up quickly, especially in September. Tours typically cost €35-55 per person. Afternoon tours (2:00-3:00 PM start) often have better light inside the cave. Wear a swimsuit under your clothes and bring a waterproof bag for your phone and valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the historic Moorish capital of the Algarve. Take a bus or train from Lagos to Silves (~30 km northeast). Visit the magnificent Castelo de Silves, a well-preserved red sandstone Moorish castle with panoramic views over the surrounding orange groves and countryside. Explore the Cathedral of Silves (Sé de Silves) adjacent to the castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves town on foot — wander through the charming whitewashed streets, browse local shops, and visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia. In the afternoon, visit a local quinta (farm estate) near Silves for an informal wine tasting and tour of the orange and almond groves that define the inland Algarve landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by early evening. Enjoy a quiet evening at the hostel or a nearby wine bar, sampling some of the wines purchased during the day.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hostel before departure (~€6-8).
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — a legendary local institution famous for its fresh seafood and cataplana. Try the cataplana de amêijoas (clam stew) or grilled tiger prawns (~€20-28 per person).
meals.dinner: Light dinner at a tapas-style wine bar in Lagos — petiscos (Portuguese tapas) including chouriço assado (grilled chorizo), queijo da serra (mountain cheese), and olives with a glass of Alentejo red wine (~€15-20 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The train from Lagos to Silves is scenic and affordable (~€3.50 each way, 40 minutes) — check CP (Comboios de Portugal) schedules. Silves is a quieter, more authentic alternative to the coastal towns and offers a fascinating glimpse into the Algarve's Moorish history. The castle entrance fee is approximately €3.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia de Dona Ana, one of Lagos's most beautiful and accessible beaches, just 2 km from the hostel (15-minute walk or short taxi). Arrive early to secure a good spot. The beach is framed by dramatic ochre cliffs and sea stacks. Swim, snorkel, and explore the small sea caves accessible at low tide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the clifftop path from Praia de Dona Ana toward Praia do Pinhão and Praia do Camilo, enjoying the stunning coastal scenery. Spend the late afternoon at whichever beach appeals most. Consider renting a stand-up paddleboard (SUP) or kayak from a beach rental operator (~€15-20 per hour).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar near Ponta da Piedade or back in Lagos old town. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a restaurant you haven't tried yet.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hostel or a café near the beach — yogurt, granola, fresh fruit, and coffee (~€7-10).
meals.lunch: Beach bar at Praia de Dona Ana — grilled fish of the day, salad, and a cold beer or fresh lemonade (~€14-18).
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Forja in Lagos — a beloved local institution serving traditional Portuguese cuisine. Try the espetada (beef skewers) or grilled black pork with migas (bread-based side dish) (~€20-26 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Dona Ana can get busy on sunny September days — arrive before 10:00 AM for the best spots. The clifftop walk between beaches is easy and well-marked. Check tide times for the best sea cave exploration at low tide. The Lagos tourist office (near Praça Gil Eanes) can provide free maps of the coastal walking paths.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha. Take a bus or taxi to Portimão (~18 km east of Lagos). Visit the Museu de Portimão, an excellent free museum housed in a former sardine canning factory, offering fascinating insights into the Algarve's fishing and canning heritage. Explore Portimão's riverside promenade and the colorful fishing boats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha, Portimão's famous beach — a wide, golden sandy beach backed by dramatic red cliffs. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing. Explore the clifftop promenade with its cafés, bars, and stunning views. Visit the Fortaleza de Santa Catarina at the eastern end of the beach for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Portimão before returning to Lagos. Portimão is famous for its grilled sardines — try them at one of the riverside restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Portimão upon arrival — coffee and a bifana (pork sandwich) or pastel de nata (~€5-7).
meals.lunch: Beach bar or café at Praia da Rocha — fresh salad, grilled fish, and a cold drink (~€14-18).
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré or Restaurante Titanic in Portimão — famous for grilled sardines (sardinhas assadas) with boiled potatoes and salad, a quintessential Algarve experience (~€15-22 per person). Return to Lagos by bus or taxi after dinner.

day_by_day.notes: The Museu de Portimão is free on Sundays but charges a small fee on other days (~€3). The bus from Lagos to Portimão runs frequently (~€3 each way, 30 minutes). Portimão is also known for its Formula 1 circuit — the Autódromo Internacional do Algarve — if motorsport interests you, check for any events during your visit.

day_by_day.morning: Guided boat trip along the Lagos coastline. Join a morning catamaran or speedboat tour departing from Lagos marina (~€35-55 per person, 2-3 hours). The tour covers the dramatic coastline between Lagos and Ponta da Piedade, including sea caves, grottos, and hidden beaches inaccessible by land. Many tours include snorkeling stops and dolphin watching opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos marina by midday. Spend the afternoon exploring the Zona Histórica (historic zone) of Lagos more thoroughly — visit the Museu Municipal Dr. José Formosinho, the Slave Market (Mercado de Escravos), and the beautiful Igreja de Santa Maria. Browse the Friday afternoon craft market if running.
day_by_day.evening: Friday evening in Lagos is lively — enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of the old town. Have pre-dinner drinks at a rooftop bar, then enjoy a special dinner at one of Lagos's better restaurants to celebrate the penultimate full day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel before the boat tour — toast, eggs, and coffee (~€6-8).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant near Lagos marina after the boat tour — try the fresh catch of the day or a seafood rice (~€16-22 per person).
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon or Dom Sebastião in Lagos — a slightly more upscale dinner to celebrate the trip. Try the lobster cataplana or grilled turbot with local Algarve wine (~€28-38 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat tour in advance from Lagos marina — multiple operators offer similar tours. Look for tours that include snorkeling equipment and a guide who explains the geological formations. September waters are warm and clear, making this an excellent time for snorkeling. The Slave Market museum (Mercado de Escravos) is historically significant — it was the first slave market in Europe, dating to 1444.

day_by_day.morning: Final wine experience — visit a local wine shop or wine bar in Lagos for a curated tasting session. Several wine shops in Lagos offer informal tastings of Algarve DOC wines, Alentejo wines, and Portuguese ports. Purchase a few bottles to take home as souvenirs. Alternatively, visit the Saturday morning market in Lagos for local produce, honey, almonds, and regional products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final beach afternoon at your favorite beach from the trip — whether Meia Praia for its long sandy expanse, Praia de Dona Ana for its dramatic cliffs, or Praia do Camilo for its intimate beauty. Soak up the last of the Algarve sunshine and warm Atlantic waters.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant from the trip, or try somewhere new. Enjoy a final evening stroll through Lagos old town, stopping for a ginjinha (cherry liqueur) or a glass of port at a traditional bar.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a café in Lagos — full Portuguese breakfast with fresh orange juice, coffee, eggs, and pastries (~€10-14).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach bar or café — keep it simple to save appetite for the farewell dinner (~€12-16).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Restaurante Dom Sebastião or O Camilo — order the full experience: amuse-bouche, fresh seafood starter, cataplana main course, and a bottle of Lagoa DOC white wine, finishing with a pastel de nata and espresso (~€30-40 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Visit the Saturday market early (before 10:00 AM) for the best selection of local products. Pack your wine purchases carefully — most airlines allow wine in checked luggage if well-wrapped. Consider purchasing local almonds, carob products, and fleur de sel (sea salt) from the Algarve as additional souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos. Check out of the hostel (standard checkout is 11:00 AM — confirm with reception). Enjoy a final coffee and pastel de nata at your favorite café. Take a last walk through Lagos old town and along the marina. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs from the craft shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, either head directly to Faro Airport or spend a few more hours in Lagos. If time allows, visit Praia de Meia Praia one last time for a final swim. Arrange your transfer to Faro Airport (approximately 1 hour by taxi or shuttle — book in advance for Sunday reliability).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days in the Algarve — stunning beaches, dramatic cliffs, excellent wines, fresh seafood, and the warm hospitality of southern Portugal.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a café near the hostel — coffee, fresh orange juice, and a croissant or tosta mista (~€6-8).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Lagos before departure, or grab food at Faro Airport if time is tight (~€10-15).
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Faro Airport or on the flight home.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Faro Airport. Pre-book your airport transfer to avoid Sunday taxi shortages. Faro Airport has a small but adequate selection of shops and restaurants for last-minute Portuguese wine and food purchases (look for Comur sardine tins, Vinho Verde, and local pastries). Confirm your flight details the night before.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim and snorkeling among the rock formations.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local wineries in the Lagoa DOC wine region, the heart of Algarve winemaking. Tour the vineyards, learn about indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco, and enjoy guided tastings of crisp whites, rosés, and robust reds paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most photographed sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos, arched rock formations, and secret beaches along the dramatic Algarve coastline, combining adventure with breathtaking natural beauty.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Local Seafood Dinner
experiences.description: Visit the windswept Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of Europe, for a dramatic Atlantic sunset. Afterward, dine at a traditional tasca in Sagres village, savoring freshly grilled cataplana (seafood stew), percebes (barnacles), and local Algarve wine in an authentic fishing village atmosphere.
experiences.location: Sagres & Cabo de São Vicente, Vila do Bispo

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Oyster Tasting
experiences.description: Take a guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park of tidal channels, barrier islands, and wildlife. Stop at a local oyster farm to taste freshly harvested oysters paired with chilled Algarve white wine, and explore the pristine barrier island beaches accessible only by boat.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer pre-arranged to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (~1 hour drive). Check in, unwind with a welcome glass of local Algarve wine left by the hotel, and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night charcuterie and cheese board from the hotel's welcome amenity, paired with a glass of Algarve white wine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private chauffeur transfer from Faro Airport to Lagos for a seamless, premium arrival experience. Confirm check-in details with the hotel in advance given the late arrival time. Keep Day 1 light – rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the hotel, then take a gentle orientation stroll through Lagos old town. Explore the historic Ponta da Bandeira Fort and the charming cobblestone streets of the city center. Visit the Igreja de Santo António, a stunning baroque church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, Lagos's longest and most elegant beach (just 10 minutes from the hotel). Rent a premium sun lounger and parasol setup, swim in the calm Atlantic waters, and enjoy the golden September sunshine. Arrange a private beach butler service if available through the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos, a beloved upscale local institution known for its fresh grilled fish, cataplana seafood stew, and extensive Portuguese wine list. Enjoy a post-dinner walk along the Lagos marina promenade.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at the hotel – fresh pastries, local cheeses, cured meats, fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch at a premium beach club near Meia Praia – grilled prawns, fresh salads, and chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina – cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana), grilled sea bass, and a bottle of Algarve Lagoa DOC white wine

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery and orientation day after the late arrival. No heavy scheduling – focus on acclimatizing to the Algarve pace and soaking in the Lagos atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim – Depart from Lagos by private car (~30 minutes east to Lagoa). Begin the iconic Praia da Marinha coastal trail, winding along dramatic golden limestone cliffs with breathtaking Atlantic views. Descend to the beach for a swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters surrounded by natural rock arches and sea stacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos) at a leisurely premium pace, stopping at hidden coves and viewpoints. Return to Lagos by private transfer. Freshen up at the hotel, then enjoy a relaxing afternoon at the hotel's lounge or rooftop area.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at No Pátio, one of Lagos's most acclaimed fine dining restaurants, set in a beautiful courtyard. Known for creative Portuguese cuisine with modern techniques, exceptional local seafood, and a curated wine list.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – fresh fruit, yogurt, local honey, pastéis de nata, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the hotel – artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, fruit, and sparkling water to enjoy on the cliffs
meals.dinner: No Pátio Lagos – tasting menu with wine pairing featuring Algarve and Alentejo wines

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. September weather is warm but manageable for hiking. The trail is moderately easy but involves some uneven terrain near cliff edges.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour – Private luxury wine tour departing from Lagos to the Lagoa DOC wine region (~20 minutes east). Visit two premium wineries such as Quinta dos Vales and Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's famous winery). Tour the vineyards, learn about the unique Algarve terroir, and enjoy guided tastings of whites, reds, and the region's celebrated rosés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine tour with a visit to a third boutique winery for a private barrel tasting and a gourmet paired lunch on the estate. Explore the wine cellar and learn about the winemaking process from the estate's sommelier. Return to Lagos by private car in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Lagos. Aperitivo hour at the hotel with a glass of local wine, then dinner at Casinha do Petisco, a refined tapas-style restaurant in Lagos known for its creative small plates and excellent Portuguese wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – full spread with local specialties
meals.lunch: Gourmet estate lunch at the winery – paired with Lagoa DOC wines, featuring local cheeses, charcuterie, and traditional Algarvian dishes
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco – premium petiscos (Portuguese tapas) including octopus carpaccio, black pork secretos, and local cheese board

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the wine tour through a premium operator for a fully private, chauffeured experience. Designate a non-drinking companion or rely on the private driver so everyone can enjoy the tastings fully. Book winery visits in advance as September is harvest season and estates can be busy.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour – Private guided kayak tour departing from Benagil Beach (~45 minutes east of Lagos by private car). Paddle through the legendary Benagil Cave, one of the world's most photographed sea caves, with its dramatic domed ceiling and natural skylight. Explore hidden grottos, sea arches, and secluded beaches accessible only by water.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil or nearby Praia do Carvalho, two of the Algarve's most beautiful and secluded beaches. Enjoy a private boat transfer back along the coast if preferred. Return to Lagos by private car. Afternoon spa treatment at the hotel or a nearby luxury spa.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar in Lagos, then dinner at Restaurante Fortaleza do Guincho (or equivalent premium Lagos restaurant) – a celebration of the day's adventures with a premium seafood feast.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – energizing spread before the active morning
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside restaurant near Benagil – grilled fish of the day, local salads, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Premium Lagos seafood restaurant – whole roasted turbot, lobster bisque, and a Grand Cru Burgundy or premium Alentejo red

day_by_day.notes: Book the private kayak tour well in advance, especially for September. Opt for a private guided tour rather than a group tour for a premium experience. Bring waterproof bags for cameras and valuables. The cave is best visited in the morning when light streams through the natural skylight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning in Lagos. Sleep in, enjoy a long hotel breakfast, then visit the Lagos Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal) for a sensory experience of fresh local produce, fish, and artisan goods. Pick up local almonds, figs, carob, and artisan jams as souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat charter from Lagos Marina for an afternoon coastal cruise along the stunning Lagos coastline. Sail past Ponta da Piedade's extraordinary rock formations, sea caves, and golden cliffs. Swim and snorkel in secluded coves accessible only by boat. Enjoy chilled champagne and canapés on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the boat as the sun sets over the Atlantic, then return to the marina. Dinner at Bon Vivant Restaurant & Lounge in Lagos – a sophisticated spot known for its creative international-Portuguese fusion cuisine and excellent cocktail program.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast followed by market exploration
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the boat – premium charcuterie, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and chilled Champagne or Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Bon Vivant Lagos – chef's tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter through the hotel concierge or a premium Lagos charter company. A 4–6 hour charter is ideal. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light layer for the sea breeze. September seas are generally calm and ideal for sailing.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres – Private car to Sagres (~45 minutes west of Lagos). Visit the imposing Fortaleza de Sagres, the historic fortress at the edge of the world where Henry the Navigator planned Portugal's Age of Discovery. Explore the dramatic windswept headland and the famous wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos).
day_by_day.afternoon: Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Local Seafood Dinner experience – Visit Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of continental Europe, for breathtaking Atlantic panoramas. Watch the dramatic waves crash against the 75-meter cliffs. Explore the lighthouse and the wild, rugged landscape. Spot migrating birds and dolphins in the waters below.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Cabo de São Vicente – one of the most spectacular sunsets in Europe as the sun dips into the Atlantic. Dinner at A Sagres or Vila Velha Restaurant in Sagres – renowned for the freshest local seafood caught that morning, including percebes (barnacles), spider crab, and grilled fish. Return to Lagos by private car.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a traditional tasca in Sagres village – fresh grilled sardines, local bread, and house wine
meals.dinner: Vila Velha Restaurant Sagres – premium seafood dinner featuring local catch, percebes, and Algarve wines, followed by the drive back to Lagos

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is notably windier and cooler than Lagos – bring a light jacket even in September. The sunset at Cabo de São Vicente is a bucket-list experience; arrive at least 30 minutes before sunset to secure a good viewpoint. The area is a UNESCO-recognized landscape.

day_by_day.morning: Spa and wellness morning at the hotel or a premium Lagos spa. Enjoy a signature Portuguese massage, facial, or hydrotherapy treatment. This is a planned rest and rejuvenation day mid-trip. Alternatively, take a yoga or meditation class if offered by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the western Algarve's hidden gem beaches by private car – visit Praia do Amado (a dramatic surf beach) and Praia da Bordeira (a vast, wild beach in the Vicentine Coast Natural Park). Walk the dunes and enjoy the untouched natural beauty of the Costa Vicentina.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a premium dinner at Restaurante Laranjeira, one of Lagos's most celebrated fine dining establishments, known for its sophisticated Portuguese cuisine, exceptional wine cellar, and intimate atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast service – fresh pastries, fruit, yogurt, and specialty coffee delivered to your room for a luxurious start
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a local restaurant near Praia do Amado – fresh fish soup, grilled catch of the day, and local wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante Laranjeira Lagos – seasonal tasting menu with premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Costa Vicentina beaches are part of a protected natural park and are significantly less crowded than the central Algarve beaches. They have a wild, dramatic beauty that contrasts beautifully with the golden limestone cliffs of the eastern Algarve. Bring a windbreaker.

day_by_day.morning: Second Algarve Wine Experience – Private visit to Quinta da Tôr or Quinta do Barranco Longo in the Loulé area, exploring the inland Algarve wine country. Enjoy a private vineyard walk during harvest season (September is peak harvest), participate in a grape picking experience, and learn about the winemaking process hands-on.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gourmet lunch at the winery estate, then explore the charming inland Algarve village of Alte, known as the 'prettiest village in the Algarve.' Wander its whitewashed streets, visit the natural spring (Fonte Grande), and browse local artisan shops for handmade ceramics and lace. Return to Lagos by private car.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktail hour at the hotel, then dinner at a premium Lagos restaurant. Try Restaurante O Camilo, perched dramatically on the cliffs above Praia do Camilo with stunning ocean views – perfect for a romantic evening dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Estate harvest lunch at the winery – traditional Algarvian dishes paired with estate wines, including local black pork, figs, and almonds
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant – fresh seafood with panoramic cliff views, paired with premium Algarve wines

day_by_day.notes: September is harvest season in the Algarve wine region – this is the absolute best time to visit wineries. The grape picking experience is a unique, hands-on luxury that most visitors never get to enjoy. Book well in advance as harvest experiences are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Oyster Tasting – Private luxury boat tour departing from Faro (~1.5 hours east of Lagos by private car). Glide through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a UNESCO-recognized protected natural park of tidal channels, barrier islands, and salt marshes. Spot flamingos, herons, and migratory birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional oyster farm within the Ria Formosa for a private oyster tasting experience directly on the water. Sample freshly harvested oysters, clams, and mussels with local white wine and lemon. Explore the barrier islands of Ilha Deserta or Ilha do Farol by boat, swimming in the calm lagoon waters.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Faro at Faz Gostos, one of the Algarve's most acclaimed fine dining restaurants, known for its creative modern Portuguese cuisine and exceptional wine list. Return to Lagos by private car after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before the early departure
meals.lunch: Oyster and shellfish tasting on the boat in the Ria Formosa – freshly harvested oysters, clams, local white wine, and artisan bread
meals.dinner: Faz Gostos Faro – premium tasting menu showcasing the best of Algarve and Portuguese cuisine

day_by_day.notes: The Ria Formosa is one of Portugal's seven natural wonders and a completely different landscape from the western Algarve cliffs. The private boat tour allows access to areas that group tours cannot reach. September is an excellent time for birdwatching as migratory species begin to arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Praia da Marinha area for a more leisurely beach day at Praia de Albandeira or Praia do Paraíso – two of the Algarve's most secluded and beautiful beaches. Arrive early to secure the best spot. Swim, snorkel, and explore the natural rock pools and sea caves on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium beach club afternoon at a luxury beach club near Armação de Pêra or Carvoeiro. Enjoy premium sun loungers, cocktail service, and a light lunch. Alternatively, arrange a private paddleboard or stand-up paddleboard session along the coast. Return to Lagos by private car.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner at the hotel's recommended top restaurant or a special reservation at a Michelin-recognized establishment. Consider Henrique Leis (if still operating) or another top Algarve fine dining destination for a truly memorable evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Premium beach club lunch – fresh seafood salads, grilled fish, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Michelin-level fine dining experience – chef's tasting menu with full wine pairing, celebrating the penultimate evening in the Algarve

day_by_day.notes: This is a day to revisit favorite spots and indulge in the Algarve's natural beauty one more time before the trip winds down. Keep the pace relaxed and luxurious.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos – slow, indulgent hotel breakfast. Last walk through Lagos old town, visiting any remaining sights such as the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos) or the beautiful Igreja de Santa Maria. Browse premium local shops for last-minute souvenirs – local wines, artisan ceramics, and Algarvian honey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final beach visit to Praia do Camilo or Praia Dona Ana, two of Lagos's most iconic and beautiful beaches, just minutes from the hotel. Enjoy a last swim in the Atlantic, soak up the September sun, and take in the stunning golden cliffs one final time.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at a premium Lagos restaurant of your choice – revisit a favorite from the trip or try one final new experience. Consider a sunset dinner at a clifftop restaurant with Atlantic views. Pack bags and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury hotel breakfast – order everything you loved during the stay
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch – fresh seafood, local salads, and a final glass of Algarve white wine
meals.dinner: Premium farewell dinner in Lagos – choose your favorite restaurant from the trip for a nostalgic final evening

day_by_day.notes: Purchase local wines, olive oils, and artisan products to bring home. The hotel concierge can arrange secure packaging for wine bottles. Confirm the departure transfer for the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final hotel breakfast. Check out of Boutique Taghostel. Private luxury transfer from Lagos to Faro Airport (~1 hour). Arrive at the airport with ample time for a comfortable, unhurried departure. Browse the airport's duty-free for last-minute Portuguese wine, pastéis de nata, and local products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days in the Algarve – dramatic cliffs, crystal waters, world-class wines, and the warmth of Portuguese hospitality.
day_by_day.evening: In transit home

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange the private airport transfer the night before. Allow at least 2 hours before departure for check-in and security at Faro Airport. The airport has a comfortable lounge accessible with premium airline tickets or Priority Pass membership – ideal for a relaxed final wait.
